newsitem.title: CHINA: China trade joint venture rules go into effect.
newsitem.headline: China trade joint venture rules go into effect.

text.p: Rules allowing foreign companies to establish trading joint ventures in some areas of China went into effect on Monday, the Xinhua news agency said.

"Beginning today, overseas businesses are allowed to join their Chinese counterparts to establish Sino-overseas foreign trade joint ventures," Xinhua quoted the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation as saying.
The State Council, China's cabinet, would decide where such ventures would be permitted to set up and how many would be permitted, the official news agency said.
At present, overseas trade joint ventures are allowed only in Shanghai's Pudong New Area and the booming Shenzhen Special Economic Zone bordering Hong Kong.
The new regulations were approved by the State Council on September 2, Xinhua said, but gave no further details.
